description: Natural-language retrieval-quality query set for the graph bake-off (P2 reopened arm). Categories: vocab = vocabulary mismatch (question shares few/no content words with the answer page); hop = answer requires link/source metadata rather than topic words; direct = topic words overlap the page. gold_fact verified against page content 2026-08-22.

queries.question: What is the risk of judging how fresh a cached fact is by when we downloaded it?
queries.gold_fact: Using ingestion time as a proxy for evidence recency produces false positives; ingestion time and evidence-effective time are two distinct clocks, only equivalent when data is created at ingestion.

queries.question: Why is waiting for something to break before acting a bad default?
queries.gold_fact: Deferral asymmetry: unchecked state claims win by default when gating on 'wait for an incident to demonstrate need' (operator correction 2026-08-14).

queries.question: How should you choose which model grades another model's answers?
queries.gold_fact: Rank verification judges on a labeled entailment probe set (ground truth known by construction, with negation, version-mismatch, and scope-overreach traps), not intuition; instrument: verifier_probe.py.

queries.question: Where does the rule that one failed test cannot end a multi-capability comparison come from?
queries.gold_fact: One-axis falsifiers cannot terminate multi-axis evaluations; the concept originated from the LightRAG bake-off premature termination incident (2026-08-22).

queries.question: A single sentence of user feedback produced the most valuable fix of the session. What principle captures this?
queries.gold_fact: Operator corrections are the highest-density signal in any session; the agent's job is to make corrections structurally permanent as fast as possible.

queries.question: Why did running the unit test suite start polluting production telemetry with fake rows?
queries.gold_fact: Wiring jsonl telemetry into a function that mock-based tests already invoke turns every pytest run into a producer of fake production rows; signal: telemetry rows with elapsed/latency exactly 0.0.

queries.question: Under time pressure the agent lists options instead of committing to one answer. What failure mode is this?
queries.gold_fact: Closure pressure: defaulting to framings that close the conversation rather than framings committing to the best answer; surface forms include trusting prior-session entries as current fact without re-probing.

queries.question: An agent wrote an architectural retirement decision into a wiki page that the operator never made. What is this called?
queries.gold_fact: Agent-fabricated architectural decisions: agents write Decision sections presenting operator-level choices (retire X, replace Y, adopt Z) as established fact, promoting inference to authority.

queries.question: Repeated re-verification of the same task keeps happening. What gap does this indicate?
queries.gold_fact: Instruction-to-state closure gap: the runtime records actions and some evidence but keeps no durable, task-scoped contract connecting the instruction, expected end state, and evidence.

queries.question: A monitoring plugin had 117 passing tests but produced zero detections in production its whole life. What was the failure class?
queries.gold_fact: The PGM plugin read the wrong payload field name in stop_detect.py, so every real session hit an empty-text guard and produced zero detections; no telemetry surfaced this.

queries.question: Why do several terminals independently retrying against the same provider quota make the outage worse?
queries.gold_fact: Independent per-session retry/failover logic creates a thundering herd on recovery; the solution is a shared coordination layer that tracks quota consumption centrally and admits dispatches before they hit 429s.

queries.question: Why is grepping the codebase the wrong receipt for claiming a script is unused and safe to delete?
queries.gold_fact: A claim that an artifact, tool, or config is 'unused' or 'safe to delete' requires a session-transcript search as its receipt; source-code grep alone is the wrong receipt type because scripts are invoked from sessions, not imported by code.

queries.question: Which investigation produced the two-clock model?
queries.gold_fact: The two-clock model came from the yt-is Evidence Fabric O-gate investigation (source field of the concept).

queries.question: What evidence standard must a claim that X causes Y meet before it is written into durable storage?
queries.gold_fact: Causal mechanism claims require source receipts before durable write; a specific high-risk form of the general claims-require-receipts rule.

queries.question: What are the failure modes of Cohere trial API keys?
queries.gold_fact: Cohere trial keys are limited to 1000 calls/month; the limit is only in the 429 body text, not headers; the UUID-looking {"id":"..."} JSON is actually a rate-limit error body.

queries.question: What are the three rules of the model pool selection policy?
queries.gold_fact: (1) Speed + adequate quota wins over free-but-slow; (2) free is a tiebreaker, not a gate; (3) model diversity overrides both for adversarial review or cross-checking.

queries.question: In what order should dispatch try providers with dedicated keys versus shared pools?
queries.gold_fact: Fleet models with dedicated API keys (Cohere, Z.ai, MiniMax, NIM, Groq, Google, Mistral) dispatch through their dedicated provider first, falling back to shared/subscription pools (OpenCode Zen/Go, OpenRouter) only when needed.

queries.question: Which hook stops malformed python one-liners before the shell mangles them, and why was a hook needed at all?
queries.gold_fact: A PreToolUse hook blocks multi-line/nested-quote python -c payloads; structural enforcement was needed because the AGENTS.md Class C prose rule has a ~50% compliance ceiling.

queries.question: What happened when an agent claimed a review lens was fired but the transcript showed it never ran?
queries.gold_fact: The /tp skill said fire all 3 lenses in parallel but the agent skipped agy, rationalizing with an unverified narrative ('we don't have a Gemini model configured') without ever running agy --version.

queries.question: How should a session close-out orchestrator skill be designed?
queries.gold_fact: Six external-sourced improvements plus five multi-terminal/stale-data invariants for a /close skill; improvements sourced from Hermes (handoff fields) and Cognizant (orchestration loop safety).
